The adManualGc flag being on is the most likely injected fault. It would force repeated full garbage collections in the ad service and degrade its performance. I did not check metrics or traces to confirm any latency or CPU impact.

flagd logged an error when loading the flag file: default variant 'on' isn't a valid variant of flag 'cartFailure'.

The root cause is an invalid feature flag configuration in flagd (cartFailure defaultVariant references a non-existent variant), which makes flagd reject the flag state. I did not check how the cart service or other services behaved with the rejected flag state, so the downstream effect is not confirmed.

claims.text: The rate service exits with a fatal error because it is not authorized on rate-db when running a count on the inventory collection.

mongodb-rate shows the rate pod (10.244.1.198) authenticating successfully as admin and then failing authorization on rate-db. This means the failure is an authorization problem, not an authentication or connectivity problem.

An earlier admin connection from 10.244.0.73 created the rate-db.inventory collection and its index at 06:13:19, so admin could write to rate-db then. The later denial is therefore not explained by the service configuration alone.

The rate crash is likely caused by the admin user in mongodb-rate lacking a readWrite role on rate-db at the time the rate service connects. I did not query the user's roles, so this is inferred from the logs only.
